 Versus

 Appearance:
 Shri R.P.Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Mithun Kulshrestha- Advocate for the respondent
 Shri Kuldeep Singh and Smt.Hemlata Shrivastava- Advo
 respondent No.3.
 Order

This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 17.05.2013 passed by Member, Additional MACT, District Lahar, District Bhind (in short "Claims Tribunal") in MACC No.32/2012 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation and also aggrieved by the finding given by the Claims Tribunal by exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of injury of the claimant, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.18,000/- has been awarded NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:16786 2 MA-869-2013 by the Claims Tribunal with interest @ 6% per annum from filing of claim petition till its realization.
Liability has been imposed upon the owner of the offending vehicle.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Claims Tribunal has committed grave error in awarding the amount and totally exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability because Sandeep Kumar vs Santosh Singh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3368956/
1 claimant is a third party and according to the insurance policy, Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation firstly to the claimant and then, it may be recovered from the owner of the offending vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that at the time of accident, injured/claimant/appellant was aged 12 years old healthy boy and he was a student.

So, notional income of appellant must be assessed as Rs.3,000/- per month, but learned Claims Tribunal has awarded the compensation on lower side,
hence, it is prayed that compensation amount be enhanced and just and reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company contended that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no enhancement.
He supported the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record it is undisputed that at the time of alleged accident, driver of of alleged vehicle was minor and he was driving the alleged vehicle without any valid driving licence, it is also undisputed that appellant/claimant was third party.

So,
in light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8, it is held that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:16786 3 MA-869-2013 the Insurance Company shall be liable to make payment of the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So, finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal with regard to totally exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability,
is not correct in the eye of law.

Therefore, finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is hereby set aside and appeal is partly allowed to the extent that Insurance Company shall pay the compensation to the claimant with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the alleged vehicle.

7. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, more particularly the age of the injured/claimant and the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident, it would be appropriate to enhance to lump sum amount of Rs.35,000/-.
8. Accordingly, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The amount of compensation is enhanced to lump sum amount of Rs.35,000/- in the present appeal.
The appellant is entitled to receive Rs.35,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of the filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
The present appeal stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
